Zizai Cast · User guide

Your phone’s screen,
on your PC.

Zizai Cast has two big features. Phone mirroring shows an iPhone, iPad or Android screen on this Windows PC; Remote control goes the other way and lets a phone control this PC. Pick one, then jump to its chapters. For mirroring, check your network in section 1 first.

Feature 1Phone mirroringShow your phone’s screen on the PC, with picture and sound (sections 1–5). Feature 2Remote controlControl your PC from a phone, at home or away (section 6).
Feature 1Phone mirroringShow your phone’s screen on the PC (sections 1–5)
iPhone · iPadScreen MirroringOne tap in Control Center, with picture and sound. Android option 1Cast (Miracast)No setup, but the PC must support wireless display. Android option 2Wireless debuggingSet up once, then control the phone with your mouse.

1Before you start

Your phone finds the PC over the network. Most “I can’t find Zizai Cast” problems come down to this section.

  1. Same Wi-Fi / local network. The phone’s Wi-Fi and the PC must be on the same router. A PC connected to that router by cable is fine too. The phone’s mobile data or personal hotspot doesn’t count.
  2. Allow the firewall on first run. When you start Zizai Cast and Windows shows a “Windows Security Alert”, tick Private networks and click Allow access. If you clicked Cancel, phones won’t find this PC (see the FAQ for the fix).
  3. Turn off VPNs. With a VPN on the PC or the phone, traffic is often routed to another network and the phone can’t see the PC. Disconnect the VPN while mirroring.
  4. School, office and hotel networks may not work. They often use “client isolation” or block device discovery, so the phone and the PC can’t see each other even on the same Wi-Fi. “Guest networks” usually behave the same way. Use your home network instead, or turn on a hotspot on the PC and connect the phone to it.
Where is Zizai Cast when it’s not on screen? Closing the window doesn’t quit the app. It stays in the background (in the system tray, the small icons next to the clock) and keeps waiting for connections. As soon as a phone connects, the window pops up again.

The waiting screen: “Pick your phone”

When no phone is connected, the window shows Pick your phone with three cards. Find the kind of phone you have and click the button on its card:

CardFor whomButton
iPhone / iPadOn the phone, open Control Center → Screen Mirroring and choose Zizai Cast.Show steps (opens section 2)
Android: view onlyUse the phone’s Cast / Smart View; you can watch but not control (Miracast).Show steps (opens section 3)
Android: control from the PCUses wireless debugging, so the PC’s mouse and keyboard can control the phone.Show QR (scan the QR code to pair, see section 4)

If a card shows small grey text, for example “Available after a restart”, it explains why that way isn’t available right now; How to connect? on the card opens this guide.

2iPhone / iPad

Uses Apple’s built-in Screen Mirroring, so there’s no app to install. Picture and sound are both sent to the PC.

Start mirroring

  1. Make sure Zizai Cast is running on the PC (the window shows “Waiting for a phone…”, or its icon is in the system tray).
  2. Open Control Center on the iPhone: on models with Face ID, swipe down from the top-right corner; on models with a Home button, swipe up from the bottom.
  3. Tap Screen Mirroring.
  4. Choose Zizai Cast from the list. Within a few seconds the phone’s screen appears on the PC with “Connected”.

Stop mirroring

Open Control Center again → Screen Mirroring → Stop Mirroring. The PC goes back to the waiting screen.

You can also disconnect on the PC: move the mouse over the mirrored screen → the red Disconnect button at the right end of the toolbar, or press CtrlD (see “How to disconnect” in section 5).

If the connection drops unexpectedly (for example the Wi-Fi cuts out), the picture dims and shows “Connection lost. Choose Screen Mirroring on the iPhone again.” Just do that.

PIN mode

Tick Ask new phones for a PIN in right-click menu → Settings (it is in the tray menu too). With it on, when a new iPhone chooses Zizai Cast for the first time, the PC shows a 4-digit PIN (“Enter this PIN on your iPhone”); the iPhone can mirror only after you enter it, and phones that succeeded are remembered.

  • Every attempt gets a different PIN; if you mistype it, the iPhone simply asks again.
  • iPhones that entered the PIN correctly are remembered and won’t be asked again.
  • Handy for PCs in shared spaces where others might connect by mistake. Changing this option while mirroring takes effect after the phone disconnects.

Several iPhones

Only one phone is shown at a time. What happens when another iPhone also chooses Zizai Cast is set in right-click menu → Settings → When a second phone connects:

OptionWhat it does
Switch to the new one (default)The new phone is shown and the previous one stops automatically. The screen shows “Switched to ‘Name’”. If a recording is running, the previous phone’s recording is saved first.
Keep the current oneThe phone that is mirroring stays; other phones are refused. Good for classes and presentations where you don’t want interruptions.

With PIN mode on, a new phone must also enter the PIN (or have been paired before) to take over.

When the screen turns off

When the iPhone locks or its screen turns off, mirroring pauses and the PC shows “iPhone screen is off”. It resumes automatically when you unlock the iPhone, with no need to reconnect. A recording keeps going through the pause.

Volume

While mirroring, the iPhone’s side volume buttons control the volume played on the PC, and Zizai Cast remembers the last level. The PC’s own system volume works as usual. No sound? See the FAQ.

3Android option 1: Cast (Miracast)

Most Android phones have built-in wireless casting (Miracast). No setup needed, but you can only watch, not control the phone from the PC, and the PC’s Wi-Fi adapter must support it.

Start casting

  1. Zizai Cast is running on the PC and its Wi-Fi is on (even if the PC is online by cable, the wireless adapter must be on).
  2. On the phone, swipe down from the top of the screen twice to open the full Quick Settings and find the casting tile (names in the table below). If it isn’t there, tap Quick Settings’ “Edit” (pencil icon) and add it.
  3. Choose Zizai Cast from the list of devices found (some phones show the PC’s name instead). The first connection may take 10–20 seconds.
  4. To stop: tap the same tile again, or pull down the notification shade and tap “Disconnect”. On the PC: Disconnect in the toolbar, or CtrlD.

Names and locations by brand

BrandQuick Settings tileOr in Settings
SamsungSmart ViewSettings → Connected devices → Smart View
Xiaomi / Redmi / POCOCast, Wireless displaySettings → Connection & sharing → Cast
OPPO / realme / OnePlusScreencast, Multi-screenSettings → Connection & sharing → Screencast
vivo / iQOOScreen mirroringSettings → Other networks & connections → Screen mirroring
ASUSWireless display, PlayToSettings → Connected devices → Connection preferences → Cast
SonyScreen mirroringSettings → Device connection → Connection preferences → Screen mirroring
Google PixelNo Miracast support (Pixel’s “Cast” only supports Chromecast, so Zizai Cast won’t appear in the list). Use option 2: wireless debugging instead.

Menu names change between system versions; the table shows the usual locations. Typing “cast”, “mirror” or “screen” into the Settings search bar usually finds it.

What the PC needs

With Miracast the phone connects straight to the PC over Wi-Fi (Wi-Fi Direct), so the PC needs a Wi-Fi adapter that supports “Wireless Display”. Most recent laptops do; a desktop with only a network cable and no Wi-Fi adapter can’t. To check:

  1. Right-click Start → Terminal (or search for “Command Prompt”).
  2. Type this line and press Enter:
netsh wlan show drivers

Look for this line in the output:

Wireless Display Supported: Yes (Graphics Driver: Yes, Wi-Fi Driver: Yes)

Both must be Yes. If you see No, try updating the Wi-Fi and graphics drivers; if it’s still No, use option 2.

Tips

  • Keep the phone fairly close to the PC with few walls in between for a steadier picture.
  • Miracast doesn’t go through the router, so the “same network” rule from section 1 doesn’t apply, but the PC’s Wi-Fi must be on.
  • With this method you can’t control the phone from the PC, only watch. To click on the phone with the mouse, use option 2.
  • Can’t connect? See Miracast won’t connect in the FAQ.

4Android option 2: Wireless debugging

Connects through Android’s built-in “Wireless debugging”. The first time takes a few minutes to set up; after that it connects automatically and you can control the phone with the PC’s mouse and keyboard. Needs Android 11 or later, and the phone and the PC must be on the same network (see section 1).

Step 1: Turn on “Developer options”

This is a hidden Android settings page. You only do this once.

  1. Open the phone’s Settings → About phone.
  2. Find Build number and tap it 7 times in a row until a message like “You are now a developer!” appears.
  3. Go back to Settings: there is now a Developer options entry (usually under “System”, or at the bottom of Settings).
BrandWhat to tapWhere Developer options is
Google Pixel and othersAbout phone → Build numberSettings → System → Developer options
SamsungAbout phone → Software information → Build numberBottom of Settings → Developer options
Xiaomi / Redmi / POCOAbout phone → All specs → MIUI version (“OS version” on HyperOS)Settings → Additional settings → Developer options
OPPO / realme / OnePlusAbout device → Version → Build numberSettings → System settings → Developer options
vivo / iQOOSystem management (About phone) → Software versionSettings → System management → Developer options

Step 2: Pair (only once)

  1. Phone: Developer options → turn on the Wireless debugging switch (the first time it asks “Allow wireless debugging on this network?”; choose Allow).
  2. PC: right-click the Zizai Cast window → Connect a phone → Connect Android (scan QR) (the “Android: control from the PC” card on the waiting screen also has a Show QR button). A QR code appears.
  3. Phone: tap the words “Wireless debugging” to open its page → Pair device with QR code, and scan the QR code on the PC with the camera frame that opens.
  4. Once paired, the pairing window closes by itself, the phone’s screen appears on the PC, and a message at the bottom says “Connected: phone name. Move the mouse to the top for the toolbar; right-click = Back”.
Stuck on “Waiting for the phone to scan…”? If there’s no answer from the phone for about 45 seconds, the window changes to “No answer from the phone: make sure it’s on the same Wi‑Fi as this PC, or use a pairing code”. Check that both are on the same network (not a guest Wi‑Fi), or click Use pairing code: on the phone tap “Pair device with pairing code”, then enter the IP address:port and the 6-digit pairing code shown on the phone into the PC and click Pair. If pairing fails, the window explains why and shows a fresh QR code automatically; just scan again.

After that: automatic reconnection

A paired phone doesn’t need to scan the QR code again. As long as the phone’s Wireless debugging is on and it’s on the same network as the PC, Zizai Cast connects automatically.

Wireless debugging turns itself off For security, many phones turn wireless debugging off after a restart or after switching Wi-Fi. Just turn it back on in Developer options; you don’t need to pair again.

Controlling the phone from the PC

On the PCOn the phone
Left-clickTap
Left-dragSwipe, e.g. turn pages or pull down the notification shade
Mouse wheelScroll up and down
Right-clickBack
Middle-click (press the wheel)Home
Typing on the keyboardTypes into the phone’s selected text field (tap the field on the phone first)

Double-clicking the black area outside the phone’s screen also toggles full screen.

Right-click is “Back”, so where is the menu? On an Android screen, right-click is sent to the phone as Back, so the Zizai Cast menu doesn’t open. To open the menu: move the mouse to the top of the screen and click ⋯ More in the toolbar (or right-click the toolbar); you can also right-click the black area outside the phone’s screen, or hold Shift and right-click (Shift + right-click always opens the menu). If you prefer right-click to open the menu, go to Settings → Right-click action and choose Open menu (the default is Back (default)); after that, use the toolbar’s Back button to go back.
Esc is sent to the phone (most apps treat it as Back); in full screen, Esc leaves full screen instead. Ctrl combinations are Zizai Cast shortcuts and aren’t sent to the phone (except CtrlC / V / X / A / Z).

Stop mirroring (disconnect)

  • PC: move the mouse over the screen → the red Disconnect button at the right end of the toolbar; or press CtrlD; or right-click the tray icon → Disconnect (phone name).
  • After disconnecting from the PC, this phone won’t reconnect automatically until you pair it again with “Connect a phone → Connect Android (scan QR)” (or restart Zizai Cast).
  • Phone: turn off Wireless debugging. When the phone turns off wireless debugging or leaves the Wi‑Fi, the PC returns to the waiting screen within a few seconds and shows “Android disconnected”.
Security note While wireless debugging is on, paired computers on the same network can access this phone. Turn wireless debugging off when you’re not mirroring, and never turn it on on public Wi-Fi. To revoke a computer’s access, remove it under “Paired devices” on the Wireless debugging page.

5Features & shortcuts

While mirroring, move the mouse over the screen and a toolbar appears at the top; right-click the window for every feature (on an Android screen right-click is Back by default, so use “More” in the toolbar or Shift + right-click; or set Settings → Right-click action to open the menu). Forgot a shortcut? Press F1 (or Help → Keyboard shortcuts) to list them all. Shortcuts work when the window is active (click it once). The app language can be switched in Settings → Language / 語言: Automatic (Windows), 繁體中文, English, 日本語, 한국어.

The toolbar while mirroring

  • It appears as soon as the mouse moves and stays while the pointer is on it; it fades out when the mouse leaves the window or stops on the picture for 2 seconds. When hidden it doesn’t cover the picture or catch clicks. The first time you connect, a hint shows where the toolbar is.
  • Hover over a button to see its name and shortcut. Clicks on the toolbar are not sent to the phone.
  • Record turns red while recording (click again to stop); More opens the full right-click menu.
  • The toolbar also has Send to phone and Freeze picture buttons (not shown in the illustration); Zoom is the magnifier and Translate is translate screen; see Magnifier, Translate and Send to phone below.

While no phone is connected, the right-click menu still lists Screenshot, Start recording, Magnifier and similar items, but greyed out with “Once a phone is connected” on the right; they become clickable when a phone connects.

How to disconnect

The same for iPhone, Android casting and wireless debugging; use any of these:

  1. The red Disconnect button at the right end of the toolbar.
  2. Press CtrlD.
  3. Disconnect at the top of the right-click menu (or of “More” in the toolbar).
  4. Right-click the tray icon → Disconnect (phone name); this works even when the app is waiting in the background.

A running recording is stopped and saved first. After an iPhone is disconnected, Screen Mirroring stops on the phone; to mirror again, choose Zizai Cast again.

Screenshot CtrlS

Saved to the 截圖 (Screenshots) folder in the install folder, with names like “ZizaiCast_<date>_<time>.png”. Right-click menu → Open screenshots folder (for recordings, Open recordings folder).

Disconnect CtrlD

Ends the current mirroring and returns to the waiting screen. Also in the toolbar (red button), the right-click menu and the tray menu.

Record CtrlR

Press again to stop. Saved as an MP4 with sound in the 錄影 (Recordings) folder. Stops and saves automatically when the phone disconnects, is taken over, or the app closes. Recording needs at least 300 MB of free disk space.

Full screen F11

Or double-click the picture. Press Esc to leave.

Always on top CtrlT

Keeps the mirroring window above other windows so you can watch the phone while you work.

Toolbar

Appears when the mouse moves over the picture: (Android: Back, Home, Recent apps) Screenshot, Record, Send to phone, Rotate, Full screen, Magnifier, Translate, Freeze, More, Disconnect.

Rotate, flip

Ctrl→ / Ctrl← rotate 90°, CtrlH flips horizontally, Ctrl0 resets. In right-click menu → View.

iPhone frame CtrlF

Draws a phone frame around the picture; with the frame on, screenshots include it too (transparent background).

Theme

Sakura, Mint, Night Sky, Milk Tea. The waiting screen and menus change colour together. Found in Settings → Theme.

Start with Windows

Waits in the background after you sign in to Windows; the window appears as soon as a phone connects. Tick it in Settings → Start with Windows (also in the tray menu); the note under the option says “Waits for phones in the background after Windows starts”.

Magnifier, high contrast, freeze

Text on the phone too small to read? Right-click the picture (on an Android screen use “More” in the toolbar, or Shift + right-click) → Magnifier. It works while a phone picture is shown.

Zoom in / out Ctrl= Ctrl-

Up to 8×. Hold Ctrl and turn the mouse wheel to zoom in where the pointer is. Back to 1×: CtrlShift0.

Move around while zoomed

Drag with the mouse (when you control an Android phone from the PC, hold Ctrl while dragging). A small overview in the bottom-right corner shows which part you’re looking at.

Magnifier button in the toolbar

Each click goes 1× → 2× → 4×, and back to 1×.

High contrast CtrlK

For low vision: Original colours, More contrast, Greyscale, Invert colours, Yellow on black. CtrlK steps through them; your choice is remembered.

Freeze picture CtrlP

Holds the current picture still on the PC so you can read it in peace, while the phone carries on as usual; press again to continue. Also a toolbar button. A recording keeps recording the live picture.

Translate the text on the screen

English, Japanese or Korean you can’t read on the phone? Right-click the picture → Translate, or click Translate in the toolbar. The translation is drawn on small cards right over the original text.

Menu itemWhat it does
Translate the whole screen CtrlLTranslates everything on the screen. Press CtrlL again to close the translation.
Translate a selected area CtrlShiftLDrag a box with the mouse; only the text inside is translated (Esc cancels).
Show original CtrlOHides the translation for a moment so you can see the original text. Greyed out until you translate; the note beside it says “Translate the whole screen first”.
Live translationTranslates again by itself when the screen changes, handy while you scroll.
Translate intoChoose 繁體中文, English, 日本語 or 한국어 (right in the first level of the Translate menu).
Show translationsAutomatic, Over the text (small cards over the original) or List, plus Dark boxes (easier to read) to make the text easier to read.
Advanced translation settingsNot needed for everyday use: offline translation works without them. Inside are Local AI translation…, Online translation (optional)… and Manage translation models (see the downloaded translation models and delete the ones you don’t need).
Works offline: the text on your screen never leaves the PC Windows’ built-in text recognition (OCR) reads the text, and the translation runs on this PC. The first time you translate a language, Zizai Cast asks first and, if you agree, downloads an offline translation model once (Mozilla Firefox Translations, MPL-2.0 licence; about 50 MB per language direction; Japanese or Korean into Traditional Chinese needs two, about 100 MB). Models are kept in %LOCALAPPDATA%\PhoneMirror\models. Text it can translate: English, Japanese, Korean and Chinese.

Japanese or Korean not translated? This PC may not be able to read that script yet. Zizai Cast then explains how to add it and offers an Open language settings button (see the FAQ).

Send to phone

After a screenshot or a recording, a small Send to phone button appears near the bottom of the picture; click it to send the file back to the phone. The right-click menu also has Send to phone ▸ Send the last screenshot to the phone, Send the last recording to the phone and Send to phone… (pick files yourself), and the toolbar has a send-to-phone button.

  • Android connected by wireless debugging: the file goes straight into the phone’s gallery. Nothing else to do.
  • iPhone / iPad, or Android casting (Miracast): a QR code appears on the PC. Scan with the phone's camera and a web page opens on the phone. Pictures: touch and hold the picture → “Save to Photos” (iPhone) or “Download image” (Android). Videos: tap “Download video” and follow the steps on the page.
  • The phone must be on the same Wi‑Fi as the PC. The link works for 10 minutes and only for whoever scans the QR code; Stop sharing ends it early.

Picture quality

Right-click menu → Settings → Picture quality. Sharper needs a stronger Wi-Fi; choose Standard if it stutters.

OptionResolutionNotes
Standard (smoothest)1080pLightest; use it on an unstable network or an older PC.
High (recommended, default)1440pThe sweet spot between sharp and smooth.
Highest (needs strong Wi-Fi)4KFor big screens and fine detail; needs a stable 5 GHz Wi-Fi.
“High” and “Highest” are greyed out? These two use the HEVC (H.265) format, which needs “HEVC Video Extensions” from the Microsoft Store to play. Without it, Standard is used automatically. After installing it, restart Zizai Cast to choose them. Picture quality currently applies mainly to iPhone / iPad mirroring. After changing Picture quality or the PIN setting, it normally applies when the current mirroring ends; Reconnect now to apply next to the hint reconnects immediately so you see the new setting right away (on an iPhone, choose Screen Mirroring again on the phone).

Background and system tray

Clicking the close button at the top right asks “Quit, or keep running in the background?”; choose Keep running in the background and Zizai Cast moves to the system tray and keeps waiting for phones (tick “Remember my choice” to skip the question; change it later in Settings → When closing the window: Ask every time / Keep running in the background / Quit). Windows 11 may hide the icon under the “^” at the bottom right; drag it onto the taskbar to pin it. Click the tray icon (or choose Show window) to bring the window back; right-click the icon to record, change settings or open folders, and while mirroring there’s also Disconnect (phone name). To really quit: right-click the tray icon → Quit.

Automatic updates

Every time Zizai Cast starts, it checks for a new version (and again every 6 hours while it runs); you can also click Check for updates in the menu. A newer installer placed in the 安裝檔 (Installers) folder inside the install folder is found automatically as well.

When a new version is out, the “A new version of Zizai Cast” window opens and lists “What’s new”, with three buttons:

ButtonWhat happens
Update nowInstalls the new version (downloading and verifying it first if needed). Zizai Cast closes, updates and opens again by itself, showing “Updated to vX.Y.Z”.
Remind me laterNothing changes now; you’ll be reminded again later.
Skip this versionNo more reminders for this version (the menu still offers it).

Zizai Cast never updates by itself and never interrupts mirroring. To update later, use Update to vX.Y.Z at the top of the menu, on the waiting screen or in the toolbar while mirroring (↑ icon). If you’re recording, it asks you first and the recording is saved.

Feature 2Remote controlControl your PC from a phone (section 6)

6Remote control: use your PC from a phone

The other way round: see this PC’s screen in the phone’s browser, hear its sound and control the mouse and keyboard with your fingers. No app to install: Safari on iPhone, Chrome on Android. At home, just scan a QR code. Away from home, we recommend a fixed address plus a password you choose: set it up once and use it every day.

Your own PC, your own phone Remote control is off by default; you turn it on yourself. While a phone is connected, a bar at the top of the PC screen says “Remote control in progress”, and you can end the session at any time with End or CtrlD.
I want to…Go to
Turn it on the first timeTurn on Remote control
Connect at home, same Wi-FiAt home: scan a QR code
Connect from outside every day (recommended)Fixed address + password
Connect from outside, Tailscale on bothTailscale
Connect from outside just once in a whileTemporary address
Hear the PC’s sound, change the volumeSound
Can’t connect, no sound, forgot the passwordTroubleshooting

Turn on Remote control

The main window has two big tabs at the top: Phone mirroring and Remote control. Switch to Remote control and turn it on. The Remote control item in the right-click menu and in the tray menu is the same switch.

Remote control is off every time Zizai Cast starts, unless you tick “Always on for outside access” below. A phone connecting for the first time must be allowed on the PC (when using the fixed address from outside this step is optional; see “Safety”).

At home: scan a QR code on the same Wi-Fi

  1. Turn on Remote control in the Remote control tab, then click Show QR code in the At home (same Wi-Fi) card.
  2. Connect the phone to the same Wi-Fi as the PC, scan the QR code with the camera and tap the link that appears (it starts with http, which is normal on a home network).
  3. The PC asks “A phone wants to control this PC”. If it is your phone, click Allow. Tick Remember this phone, don’t ask again so you aren’t asked again.
  4. The PC’s screen appears on the phone. To hear the PC’s sound, tap Turn on sound at the bottom (iPhone requires a tap before any sound plays).
  5. Turn the phone sideways for the largest picture. For full screen, add the page to your Home Screen.

Away from home (recommended): fixed address + your own password

The easiest way to reach your PC from outside is the fixed address: the address never changes, and you sign in with a password you set yourself. Nothing to install on the phone; saved to the Home Screen it behaves like an app.

MethodAddressNeeded on the phoneWho must be at the PC
Fixed address (recommended)Never changesNothingDuring setup only
TailscaleFixed (Tailscale address)The Tailscale appNobody
Temporary addressChanges every timeNothingSomeone must press Allow every time
  1. The first time, set a password on the PC. In the Remote control tab click Set password in the Away: fixed address + password card and type your password twice, at least 8 characters. The password can only be set on the PC, never from the phone.
  2. Tick Always on for outside access (works from the moment the PC starts). After that, once the PC is on and you are signed in, you can connect from outside without turning anything on first.
  3. Open the fixed address on the phone and enter the password. The address is shown in the PC window; copy it and send it to yourself, or scan its QR code.
  4. Add the page to your Home Screen, and from then on just tap the icon.
5 wrong passwords in a row lock it for 15 minutes After 5 wrong passwords in a row, sign-in is locked for 15 minutes, even with the right password. Nothing is broken; wait 15 minutes and try again.

Add the page to your Home Screen

Once added, a “Zizai Remote” icon appears on the Home Screen. It opens without an address bar, full screen, like an app.

  • iPhone: open the page in Safari, tap Share → Add to Home Screen.
  • Android: open the page in Chrome, tap the menu at the top right → Add to Home screen.
Screenshot to be addediPhone: Share → Add to Home Screen
Screenshot to be addedAndroid: menu → Add to Home screen

Away from home: Tailscale

If you already use Tailscale (free; it joins your own PC and phone into a private network only you can enter), you can use it to reach home as well. Zizai Cast changes none of Tailscale’s settings. The phone needs the Tailscale app, which is the main difference from the fixed address.

  1. PC: download and install Tailscale from https://tailscale.com/download and sign in with a Google, Microsoft or Apple account.
  2. Phone: install “Tailscale” from the App Store or Google Play, sign in with the same account and switch it on.
  3. On the PC, turn Remote control off and on again (or restart Zizai Cast); click Show QR code in the Away: Tailscale card to get its QR code (the address starts with 100.).
  4. While at home, scan this QR code with the phone and add it to the Home Screen; from outside, open it from the icon (Tailscale must be on on the phone).
Mobile data The “Sharp” quality (the PC’s native resolution) uses about 10 Mbps, roughly 4 GB per hour. Choose Smooth in the phone’s settings to save a lot; almost nothing is sent while the picture is still. With Adjust quality automatically on, quality drops by itself when the network is poor.
  • No QR code in the “Away: Tailscale” card: Tailscale on the PC is off or signed out. Fix that, then turn Remote control off and on again.
  • The phone can’t open the address: Tailscale on the phone is off, or the two are signed in to different accounts.
  • Connects but is choppy: switch the quality to “Smooth” in the phone’s settings; a weak mobile signal also causes this.

Away from home: temporary address

For a quick one-off, without setting a password or leaving anything running, use a temporary address. Zizai Cast uses a free Cloudflare address (cloudflared) that needs no account (https://…trycloudflare.com). The address changes every time, and someone has to be at the PC to press Allow every time.

  1. PC: in the Remote control tab click More settings → No-app link (the phone connects from mobile data too). After about 10–20 seconds a small window shows a QR code and a 6-digit passcode.
  2. Scan the QR code with the phone’s camera (each QR code works only once; the PC replaces it after use) and enter the passcode.
  3. The PC shows an Allow window. Someone at the PC clicks Allow and can tick Remember this phone, don’t ask again.
  4. Do this once beside the PC before you leave. If the network drops while you are out, the page reconnects by itself with no new Allow and no passcode. But when the PC restarts or the temporary address is restarted, the address changes and you must scan again.
Three layers of protection A one-time link (valid 10 minutes, usable once) + the passcode (5 wrong entries void that link; 10 from one address block it for 15 minutes) + Allow on the PC. Click Stop the link when you are done; turning Remote control off or quitting Zizai Cast stops it too.
  • The top right of the phone page shows Direct · 23 ms or Tunnel · 85 ms: it first tries a direct connection between phone and PC (fastest); if that fails it switches to the Cloudflare tunnel after about 2.5 seconds. The number is the round-trip delay.
  • If the tunnel is too slow, the PC lowers the bitrate and skips frames it can’t send in time, so the delay doesn’t pile up.
  • Showing the picture over the tunnel needs a recent Safari or Chrome (WebCodecs); an older browser explains why it can’t.

Gestures

Three buttons sit at the bottom right of the page: sound, keyboard, settings. In settings choose Trackpad (default, like a laptop’s) or Direct (tap where you want to click), set the Pointer speed (faster swipes go further), pick the picture quality, or lock the zoom.

GestureWhat it does
One fingermove the pointer
Tapleft click
Two-finger tapright click
Two fingers up/down/sidewaysscroll
Hold still for half a second, then movedrag (select text, move windows)
Pinchzoom the picture; while zoomed move two fingers to pan; the zoom button at the bottom right goes back to “Fit to screen”
Three-finger tapkeyboard on / off
Direct modetap where you want to click; hold half a second = right click; touch and move = drag

Keyboard panel: typing on the phone keyboard (any input method) types on the PC; plus Ctrl / Alt / Shift / Win, Esc, Tab, arrows, Copy, Paste, Select all, Task view, File Explorer, Snip, Task Manager and Close window (Alt+F4, asks first). Clipboard sends text from the phone to the PC clipboard, or brings text copied on the PC to the phone.

Sound

The phone page plays the PC’s sound. Tap Turn on sound on the page (iPhone requires a tap).

  • The sound of all speakers is mixed together and sent to the phone. However many playback devices the PC has (speakers, monitor, headphones, Bluetooth), the phone hears them all; there is no device to choose.
  • The phone page has a volume control, 0–300%. If the PC is too quiet, raise it above 100% to boost it.
  • To keep the PC quiet, tick “Mute the PC while the phone plays sound”. While the phone is playing, the PC’s speakers stay silent; they return to normal when the phone disconnects.
  • Switch the speakers off and the phone still has sound. The phone gets the sound before it reaches the speakers, so powering them off or unplugging them makes no difference.
The phone goes silent when the PC is muted? “Mute the PC while the phone plays sound” uses the same speaker mute as Windows; on the devices tested the phone keeps its sound while the PC is muted. A few sound cards mute before the sound can be picked up; if yours does, switch the speakers off instead.

Safety

The fixed address is public. Your password is the only protection Anyone who knows the address can see the sign-in page; only your password keeps them out. Use a password that is long and not used anywhere else (at least 8 characters, longer is better; for example three or four unrelated words strung together). Don’t keep the address and the password in the same place.
  • You can require Allow on the PC for new phones. Turn on More settings → New phones from outside also need Allow on the PC (off by default): a new phone coming in from outside must, after the right password, also be allowed by someone at the PC. Don’t turn it on when you are away from the PC (nobody could press Allow); turn it on if you are usually at the PC and want one more lock.
  • You can end a session at any time. While connected, the top of the screen always shows ● Remote control in progress with a View only switch and End (Ctrl+D). CtrlD works from any program. A phone that was disconnected has to connect again.
  • 5 wrong passwords in a row lock sign-in for 15 minutes.
  • View only: the phone can look but can’t move the mouse or type.
  • A session ends by itself after 30 minutes without a touch (adjustable). The PC does not sleep while connected. Every connection is logged with its source IP.
  • More settings → Remembered phones: click one to forget it, or use Forget remembered phones to clear them all.
  • When you no longer need outside access, untick Always on for outside access (works from the moment the PC starts) so the fixed address is no longer open.

Limits: what it can’t do

  • Windows running as administrator (for example Task Manager, some installers), UAC prompts and the lock screen (including the Ctrl+Alt+Del screen) can’t be operated from the phone. This is a Windows security rule; handle those at the PC.
  • The PC must be on and signed in. If it is shut down, asleep or sitting at the sign-in screen, the phone can’t connect.
  • The fixed address needs Tailscale running on the PC. If Tailscale on the PC is off or signed out, the fixed address won’t open (the phone doesn’t need it). Your Tailscale account must also allow Funnel; when it can’t be used, the fixed address card says why in plain words and offers Use a temporary address (still with your password, but the address changes after a restart).
  • Only one phone can be connected at a time.

Remote control troubleshooting

No sound
  • Tap Turn on sound on the page (always needed on iPhone), and check the iPhone’s silent switch and volume.
  • Check that the page’s volume control isn’t at 0%; it goes up to 300%.
  • The PC may really be playing nothing: the page then says “The PC is not playing any sound right now”.
  • Windows mute is on: turn Windows mute off. To keep the PC quiet use “Mute the PC while the phone plays sound” or switch the speakers off.
Can’t connect
  • The QR code at home doesn’t open: the phone isn’t on the same Wi-Fi (guest network or mobile data), or the router has “AP isolation” on. Join the PC’s Wi-Fi or turn AP isolation off.
  • The fixed address doesn’t open: check that the PC is on and signed in, that Tailscale is running on it, and that “Always on for outside access (works from the moment the PC starts)” is ticked.
  • Right password but it won’t let you in: did you get it wrong 5 times in a row? It is locked for 15 minutes; try again afterwards.
  • The page opens but says “Video connection blocked”: Windows Firewall is blocking Zizai Cast (click “Allow access” the first time you turn Remote control on), the router has AP isolation, or another VPN is on at the PC or phone.
  • The phone says “This address is no longer valid”: the pairing code in settings.ini was deleted or Zizai Cast was reinstalled. Scan the QR code again (and add the Home Screen icon again).
  • It connects but waits for Allow: you turned on “New phones from outside also need Allow on the PC”, or this is a new phone. Someone at the PC has to click Allow.
I forgot the password

Reset it on the PC: open the Remote control tab and set a new password for the fixed address (at least 8 characters). It can’t be reset from the phone, on purpose: only someone sitting at the PC can change it. After a reset, the phone has to sign in again with the new password.

Some windows don’t react

Windows running as administrator (such as Task Manager), UAC prompts, the lock screen and the Ctrl+Alt+Del screen can’t be operated from the phone. Handle those at the PC.

7FAQ

Click a question to see the answer. This FAQ is about phone mirroring; remote control troubleshooting is at the end of section 6.

“Zizai Cast” doesn’t appear in the phone’s list
  • No sound in Remote control: tap “Turn on sound” on the phone page (always on iPhone), check its volume isn’t 0%, and don’t use Windows mute. See “No sound” under Remote control.
  • Make sure Zizai Cast is running (its icon is in the system tray).
  • The phone and the PC are on the same Wi-Fi, not a guest network, and the phone isn’t using mobile data.
  • Turn off VPNs on the PC and the phone.
  • Make sure the firewall allows Zizai Cast (see “Firewall” below).
  • School, office and hotel networks may block device discovery; try another network.
  • Only one AirPlay receiver can run on a PC; if you have AirServer, UxPlay, LonelyScreen or similar, close it first.
  • Turn the phone’s Wi-Fi off and on again, or restart Zizai Cast.
Picture, but no sound
  • Turn up the iPhone’s volume with its buttons, and check that the Ring/Silent switch isn’t on silent (some apps stay quiet in silent mode).
  • Check the volume at the bottom right of the PC, and that Zizai Cast isn’t muted in the Volume mixer.
  • Make sure the Windows default output device is the speaker or headphones you’re listening to. After switching headphones, reconnect once.
  • Some apps (for example some streaming services) block picture or sound during screen mirroring for copyright protection. That isn’t a Zizai Cast problem.
The picture lags or stutters
  • Wi-Fi signal matters most. Put both the phone and the PC on 5 GHz Wi-Fi near the router, or connect the PC by cable.
  • Temporarily set Picture quality to “Standard (smoothest)”.
  • Close programs that are downloading or uploading a lot (cloud sync, game updates, etc.).
  • A very short delay during normal use is expected; with videos, picture and sound are sent together.
The picture is blurry
  • Right-click menu → Settings → Picture quality, choose “High (recommended)” or “Highest (needs strong Wi-Fi)”. If they’re greyed out, install “HEVC Video Extensions” from the Microsoft Store.
  • A Picture quality change normally takes effect from the next connection (while mirroring, it waits until the phone disconnects); to apply it right away click “Reconnect now to apply” next to the hint.
  • On an unstable network the phone lowers the quality by itself, so a briefly blurry picture is normal.
Someone else’s phone took over in the middle of mirroring
  • Right-click menu → Settings → When a second phone connects, choose “Keep the current one”; other phones then can’t connect while you’re mirroring.
  • You can also turn on “Ask new phones for a PIN”; phones that haven’t entered the PIN can’t mirror.
Firewall: I clicked “Cancel”. What now?
  1. Start → search for “Allow an app through Windows Firewall” and open it.
  2. Click Change settings, find “Zizai Cast” in the list and tick Private (also tick Public if you use it on public networks).
  3. If it isn’t in the list, click Allow another app… and choose 程式\自在投影.exe in the install folder.
  4. If another antivirus product has its own firewall, allow Zizai Cast there too.

Also, if Windows has your home network set as a “Public network”, more is blocked. You can change it to “Private network” in Settings → Network & internet → Wi-Fi → your network.

It won’t connect while a VPN is on

A VPN routes network traffic elsewhere, so the phone and the PC are no longer on the “same network”. Disconnect the VPN on the PC and the phone while mirroring. Some VPNs have an “Allow local network access” (Local network sharing / LAN access) option; with it on, they can be used together.

Android casting (Miracast) won’t connect
  • First check with netsh wlan show drivers that the PC supports “Wireless Display” (see section 3).
  • The PC’s Wi-Fi must be on, and its Mobile hotspot must be off.
  • Stuck on “Connecting”: cancel on the phone, wait 10 seconds and try again; or turn the phone’s Wi-Fi off and on.
  • Some PCs’ adapters support it but don’t get along with certain phones. Update the Wi-Fi driver, or use option 2: wireless debugging.
  • Google Pixel doesn’t support Miracast; use option 2 directly.
Wireless debugging keeps disconnecting, or doesn’t reconnect next time
  • After the phone restarts or switches Wi-Fi, the system often turns wireless debugging off. Turn it back on in Developer options; no need to pair again.
  • The phone’s battery saver may cut Wi-Fi when the screen is off. Turn battery saver off in the battery settings, or exclude “Settings” from battery optimization.
  • Make sure the phone and the PC are still on the same network and no VPN is on.
  • Still not working: remove this PC under “Paired devices” on the phone, then pair again with “Connect a phone → Connect Android (scan QR)”.
  • A phone disconnected with the toolbar or CtrlD won’t reconnect automatically; connect it again with “Connect a phone → Connect Android (scan QR)”, or restart Zizai Cast.
I can’t find “Disconnect”

Move the mouse over the mirrored screen: a toolbar appears at the top centre, and the red button at its right end is Disconnect. You can also press CtrlD, or right-click the tray icon → Disconnect (phone name). On an Android screen right-click means “Back” by default, so it doesn’t open a menu; use “More” in the toolbar, press Shift + right-click, or set Settings → Right-click action to “Open menu”.

Translation does nothing, or Japanese / Korean isn’t translated
  • The first translation needs a one-time download: when Zizai Cast asks, click Download (once only; about 50 MB per language direction, about 100 MB for Japanese or Korean into Traditional Chinese). With Not now nothing is translated, and you’ll be asked again next time.
  • Japanese / Korean text isn’t recognised: Windows needs the “Optical character recognition” feature of that language. Click Open language settings in the message, or open Windows Settings → Time & language → Language & region → Add a language → Japanese (or Korean) → Next, tick only “Optical character recognition” (no display language, no language pack) → Install. Then translate again.
  • Translation works while a phone picture is shown. Downloaded models can be seen or deleted under Translate → Manage translation models.
Is the app still running after I close the window?

Yes, it stays in the background (in the system tray at the bottom right). To quit completely, right-click the tray icon → Quit. If you don’t want it to start with Windows, untick “Start with Windows”.
